text:
Evidence supports testing the ranking objective first, but does not establish it as Electronics’ main bottleneck. [eSASRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06450) identifies sampled softmax plus LiGR layers as a strong SASRec configuration; its SASRec+sampled-softmax comparison also motivates an objective-only ablation. [Negative-sampling experiments (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) find substantial dataset dependence: uniform sampling favors aggregate accuracy and head items, while popularity-based sampling can improve balance at an accuracy cost. Neither result proves superiority under this benchmark’s sampled HR@10.

Hard negatives warrant gradual introduction. [R2NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) combines uniform warm-up, global candidate recall, and curriculum sampling from top-ranked candidates; it highlights early training instability and false negatives from always selecting the highest-scoring unseen item. Practical ablation: retain uniform negatives, gradually add negatives sampled randomly from a top-M pool, and exclude known training positives. Unobserved items remain unlabeled; model scores cannot establish that they are true negatives.

For nonuniform or in-batch negatives, correction must match the actual proposal distribution. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) accounts for the positive being included deterministically and introduces uncertainty-based weighting; blanket subtraction of log-popularity is insufficient. Suggested search order, as an experimental inference: uniform multi-negative BCE versus sampled-softmax/InfoNCE with tuned temperature; then corrected mixed sampling; then warm-start hard mining with false-negative downweighting. Hold architecture and training budget comparable, inspect category results, and select exclusively by unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10. Electronics’ higher pair error motivates this comparison but does not diagnose its cause.
